page: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8124M processor with 36 physical cores and 72 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 24 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX and AVX-512F. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 2.67 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities and high memory bandwidth. The instance achieves a strong multi-core CPU performance score of 66660.83 in stress-ng and a PassMark CPU score of 49891.05. Memory read bandwidth is robust, reaching 3704.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 208.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, write bandwidth for large blocks is average at 90.55 GB/sec. Single-core performance and web serving throughput fall into the average tier, while large language model text generation performance is weak, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

A key differentiator of the c5n.18xlarge is its 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, which facilitates high-throughput data transfers and efficient EBS communication. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of dedicated compute resources and high-speed networking without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPUs. This profile makes it highly suitable for network-bound compute workloads, distributed database operations, multi-threaded batch processing, and high-performance computing applications that require significant network throughput but do not rely on hardware acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized, network-optimized instance featuring 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this x86_64 instance includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. It delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, making it highly efficient for network-intensive applications. Benchmark data shows strong multi-core CPU performance and high memory read bandwidth, though single-core execution and LLM text generation remain average to weak. Qualitatively, the instance provides high compute density and network throughput without the overhead of local storage. It is best suited for high-performance computing, distributed database operations, and network-bound batch processing workloads.
